problem: "If the output decays, raise Kp. If it grows, lower Kp." A student can read "grows" as the output value rising to a new steady level, which happens with almost any P gain, rather than the oscillation amplitude growing. The action-word pair is also easy to mix up.
fix: Write: "If the oscillation amplitude decays, raise Kp. If the oscillation amplitude grows cycle by cycle, lower Kp."

problem: Ti and Td belong to the standard (ideal) form Kp(1 + 1/(Ti s) + Td s) as well as to the series (interacting) form; calling Kp, Ti, Td the "series-form settings" is not the usual naming and can confuse a student meeting the three forms for the first time.
fix: Write: "Do not mix parallel-form gains (Kp, Ki, Kd) with standard-form settings (Kp, Ti, Td) without converting. The series (interacting) form uses the same Ti and Td but a different Kp."
